beats.narration_text: This is a Final Project Pitch Film created by Ethan Gomes. The project is called Data Sentry. Nothing is built yet; everything here is a plan. The question isn't whether Claude can write data checks. It's whether anyone can measure what they miss.

shot.visual_intent: Title card: 'DataSentry' large and centred; a thin rule draws beneath it with one terracotta dot; one line below: 'Scoring AI-written data checks with planted defects'.
shot.motion_claim: Title card: 'DataSentry' large and centred; a thin rule draws beneath it with one terracotta dot; one line below: 'Scoring AI-written data checks with planted defects'.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell: one drawn object on a cream stage, a label or two; the voice explains. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Three terms. A data check: a rule a table must pass. A planted defect: a mistake put into a copy of the data on purpose. And a catch rate: the share of planted defects the checks find.

terms.meaning: a rule a table must pass, like no missing fares
a mistake put into a copy of the data on purpose
the share of planted defects the checks find

qc.sparse_reason: TERMS card: three prerequisites, one line each.

beats.narration_text: Data Sentry will be a workflow, built in Claude Code, that writes data checks for a table, then scores those checks by planting defects they have to catch.

shot.visual_intent: A checkpoint scanner arch lands on the stage with its floor shadow; the name 'DataSentry' sits beside it; a parcel (the table) slides under the arch.
shot.motion_claim: A checkpoint scanner arch lands on the stage with its floor shadow; the name 'DataSentry' sits beside it; a parcel (the table) slides under the arch.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell: one drawn object on a cream stage, a label or two; the voice explains. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: When it's done, it will be a public GitHub repo with three parts: a check writer, a defect planter, and a scorecard of what was caught and what was missed.

shot.visual_intent: A kraft crate (the repo) opens; three parts rise beside it one by one, a check page, a dark planter block, a binder; each labelled once.
shot.motion_claim: A kraft crate (the repo) opens; three parts rise beside it one by one, a check page, a dark planter block, a binder; each labelled once.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell: one drawn object on a cream stage, a label or two; the voice explains. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: It will start from public data, for example one month of New York City yellow taxi trips, about ten thousand rows. Pick-up time, drop-off time, passengers, distance, and fare.

shot.visual_intent: A flat table card lands; five column headers block in; grey rows stack down it as the columns are named.
shot.motion_claim: A flat table card lands; five column headers block in; grey rows stack down it as the columns are named.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell: one drawn object on a cream stage, a label or two; the voice explains. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Claude Code will see only the column names and types, and write checks in pandera, an open-source Python library for testing data frames. It will never see the list of defects.

shot.visual_intent: An agent workstation; check pages drop beside it; at right a sealed box marked 'defect list' sits behind a closed barrier.
shot.motion_claim: An agent workstation; check pages drop beside it; at right a sealed box marked 'defect list' sits behind a closed barrier.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell: one drawn object on a cream stage, a label or two; the voice explains. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Separately, a plain Python script will copy the clean sample and break it five ways: duplicates, missing values, impossible numbers like a negative fare, a drop-off before its pick-up, and the wrong type.

shot.visual_intent: Two table cards side by side, clean and broken copy; five terracotta marks land on the broken copy, one per defect named.
shot.motion_claim: Two table cards side by side, clean and broken copy; five terracotta marks land on the broken copy, one per defect named.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell: one drawn object on a cream stage, a label or two; the voice explains. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Then every check runs twice. On the clean copy, it must pass. On the broken copy, it must fail. Out comes a catch rate for each kind of defect, with every miss written down.

shot.visual_intent: The scanner from B00; the clean parcel rides through and gets a check; the broken parcel is stopped at the arch with a terracotta light.
shot.motion_claim: The scanner from B00; the clean parcel rides through and gets a check; the broken parcel is stopped at the arch with a terracotta light.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell: one drawn object on a cream stage, a label or two; the voice explains. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Why would anyone care? I looked at two tools data teams already use. First, D B T. Its built-in tests check exactly what you write: unique, not null, accepted values, relationships.

shot.visual_intent: Two comparison trays; the left tray fills with four small test blocks, one per built-in test named; label 'dbt'.
shot.motion_claim: Two comparison trays; the left tray fills with four small test blocks, one per built-in test named; label 'dbt'.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell: one drawn object on a cream stage, a label or two; the voice explains. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: The second is Great Expectations. Its paid G X Cloud has a feature, Expect A I, that suggests checks for you to review and approve. So AI-suggested checks already exist.

shot.visual_intent: The right tray fills with suggested check pages; an approval stamp comes down on the top page; label 'GX Cloud'.
shot.motion_claim: The right tray fills with suggested check pages; an approval stamp comes down on the top page; label 'GX Cloud'.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell: one drawn object on a cream stage, a label or two; the voice explains. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: What I didn't find, in what I read, was a way to measure how good those checks are. Data Sentry will tell a data engineer which bad rows their checks would let through.

shot.visual_intent: Both trays stay; a broken parcel with a terracotta mark slides past both trays untouched; a question-mark tag lands beside it.
shot.motion_claim: Both trays stay; a broken parcel with a terracotta mark slides past both trays untouched; a question-mark tag lands beside it.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell: one drawn object on a cream stage, a label or two; the voice explains. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Who opens it? A hiring manager for a data engineering role. In the first minute, they'll run one command on a broken file and see each defect type: caught, or missed.

shot.visual_intent: A terminal window (dark title bar) opens; a cursor types one grey command bar; five result rows land with a mark each; tagged 'constructed'.
shot.motion_claim: A terminal window (dark title bar) opens; a cursor types one grey command bar; five result rows land with a mark each; tagged 'constructed'.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell: one drawn object on a cream stage, a label or two; the voice explains. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: What would it prove? Four skills from this class: a prompt contract for each check, an agent loop that writes, runs, and revises, verification against a clean copy, and evaluation by catch rate.

shot.visual_intent: An evidence binder; its cover opens; four record sheets fan out in a row with ink numerals 1 to 4, one per skill named.
shot.motion_claim: An evidence binder; its cover opens; four record sheets fan out in a row with ink numerals 1 to 4, one per skill named.

beats.narration_text: Once it's built, a reviewer could fairly conclude that I test an AI's output instead of trusting it. The evidence will be in the repo: the scorecard, the log of every round, and the prompts behind each check.

shot.visual_intent: A review desk; a check mark lands with 'tested, not trusted'; then three pieces of planned evidence (scorecard binder, log sheet, prompt page) slide onto the desk; tagged 'planned evidence'.
shot.motion_claim: A review desk; a check mark lands with 'tested, not trusted'; then three pieces of planned evidence (scorecard binder, log sheet, prompt page) slide onto the desk; tagged 'planned evidence'.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell: one drawn object on a cream stage, a label or two; the voice explains. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: In scope: one table, five defect types, one scorecard. Out of scope, on purpose: orchestration, so no Airflow. First to run: one defect, one check, one printed line. If it prints, it ran.

shot.visual_intent: A task queue; the waiting tasks stay ghosted; the next task slides forward onto the rail, a single printed line appears beside it with a check; label 'first run'.
shot.motion_claim: A task queue; the waiting tasks stay ghosted; the next task slides forward onto the rail, a single printed line appears beside it with a check; label 'first run'.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell: one drawn object on a cream stage, a label or two; the voice explains. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: What could sink it? Checks that are too loose. A check that passes everything catches nothing, and the score would still look fine. So the clean copy and the broken copy are both required, every time.

shot.visual_intent: A permission gate with its barrier raised; a broken parcel rides straight through; then the barrier comes down and the next broken parcel stops.
shot.motion_claim: A permission gate with its barrier raised; a broken parcel rides straight through; then the barrier comes down and the next broken parcel stops.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell: one drawn object on a cream stage, a label or two; the voice explains. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Why this project? It will help me land a data job, like a Data Engineer or Data Analyst role. It will highlight the skills I'm working on: Python, pandas, pandera, and Claude Code in a loop that fixes its own checks.

shot.visual_intent: A tray labelled 'working on' fills with four skill blocks, one per skill named; an arrow draws from the tray to the hiring manager's desk (from B10A), labelled 'Data Engineer' and 'Data Analyst'.
shot.motion_claim: A tray labelled 'working on' fills with four skill blocks, one per skill named; an arrow draws from the tray to the hiring manager's desk (from B10A), labelled 'Data Engineer' and 'Data Analyst'.
